About Moomoo Financial Canada Inc. (MFC) 
 Having launched in Canada just over a year ago, MFC has experienced significant growth and success. Based in Toronto, with convenient access to the city’s Line 1 TTC subway, our new office boasts bright, open spaces and spectacular views of the city. As we continue to scale, we are seeking to expand our team with a dynamic, growth-mindset Investment Representative.
 About the Role 
 Part-Time with Potential to Transition to Full-Time 
 We are looking for a proactive and resourceful Procurement Specialist to support and strengthen our Canadian procurement function.
 This role will initially be structured on a part-time basis , with strong potential to transition into a full-time position as our Canadian operations and procurement needs continue to grow.
 The successful candidate will play an important role in connecting our Canadian business with our Headquarters Procurement team . This person will be expected to learn and understand our global procurement processes, navigate the complexities of cross-border collaboration, and help ensure that local Canadian business needs are addressed effectively within the broader corporate procurement framework.
 At the same time, we are looking for someone who can bring strong Canadian market knowledge and local expertise in procurement, vendor management, sourcing, and contract administration . The role requires someone who can balance global processes with local requirements and help build practical, efficient, and scalable procurement practices for Canada.
 The ideal candidate is organized, commercially minded, solutions-oriented, and comfortable working across different teams, cultures, processes, and time zones. Mandarin Chinese is considered a strong asset given the significant interaction with our Headquarters team. 
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Learn, understand, and become a local subject matter resource on the company’s global procurement policies, procedures, approval workflows, and systems.
 Serve as a key liaison between the Canadian business and the Headquarters Procurement team, ensuring clear communication, timely follow-up, and effective coordination of procurement activities.
 Help navigate and resolve complexities arising from cross-border procurement processes, including differences in local business practices, vendor requirements, documentation, timelines, and approval processes.
 Translate Canadian business requirements into clear procurement requests that can be effectively processed through global procurement channels.
 Provide local expertise and guidance on Canadian sourcing, vendor selection, purchasing practices, contract administration, and supplier management.
 Source, identify, and evaluate local Canadian vendors and service providers based on cost, quality, service capability, compliance, reliability, and business requirements.
 Manage quotation and proposal processes, including gathering requirements, obtaining competitive bids, conducting comparisons, and supporting vendor selection.
 Coordinate vendor onboarding, including collection and review of required business information, banking details, contracts, compliance documentation, and internal approvals.
 Support the end-to-end contract management process, including coordination with vendors, Legal, Finance, business stakeholders, and Headquarters teams.
 Maintain visibility over contract terms, renewal dates, service periods, pricing arrangements, and key vendor obligations.
 Help ensure that contracts and procurement arrangements reflect Canadian business, regulatory, operational, and commercial requirements.
 Track procurement requests from initiation through approval, purchase, contract execution, delivery, invoicing, and completion.
 Maintain organized and accurate procurement records, vendor files, contracts, quotations, purchase documentation, and approval records.
 Partner with Finance on invoice processing, payment coordination, vendor setup, and reconciliation of procurement-related documentation.
 Monitor vendor performance and support the resolution of service, delivery, pricing, contract, or invoicing issues.
 Build productive relationships with local vendors and internal stakeholders while maintaining appropriate procurement controls and independence.
 Identify gaps, inefficiencies, or communication issues in the procurement process and recommend practical improvements.
 Help improve transparency, turnaround time, accountability, and stakeholder experience across Canada–HQ procurement activities.
 Support procurement needs across functions including IT, Marketing, Compliance, Operations, Office Administration, Finance, and other corporate functions.
 Contribute to the ongoing development of a scalable Canadian procurement function as the organization grows.
 Diploma or degree in Supply Chain Management, Procurement, Business Administration, Finance, Operations , or a related field.
 Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in procurement, sourcing, purchasing, vendor management, contract administration, supply chain, or a related function.
 Hands-on experience managing vendor relationships, sourcing activities, quotations, proposals, contracts, purchase requests, and vendor onboarding.
 Strong knowledge of Canadian procurement practices, local vendors, supplier management, and commercial practices .
 Experience supporting or managing contract lifecycle activities , including contract coordination, renewals, pricing terms, vendor obligations, and documentation.
 Experience working within a multinational organization or coordinating with an overseas headquarters or regional procurement team is strongly preferred.
 Demonstrated ability to learn and navigate complex corporate procurement processes, policies, approval workflows, and systems.
 Strong understanding of the challenges associated with cross-border collaboration , including differences in business practices, communication styles, processes, timelines, and local requirements.
 Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to identify process gaps, work through ambiguity, and develop practical solutions.
 Strong commercial judgment and the ability to evaluate vendors based on pricing, quality, service capability, reliability, risk, and overall business value.
 Excellent stakeholder-management and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with local business teams, Headquarters functions, Finance, Legal, and external vendors.
 Strong organizational and project-management skills with the ability to manage multiple procurement activities, deadlines, and priorities simultaneously.
 Excellent attention to detail, particularly when reviewing contracts, pricing, vendor documentation, approval records, and payment information.
 Comfortable working independently and taking ownership of procurement matters from initiation through completion.
 Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook .
 Fluency in English is required.
 Mandarin Chinese is strongly preferred due to frequent interaction and collaboration with our Headquarters Procurement team.
 WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR 
 We are looking for someone who is not only able to execute procurement activities, but who can also build capability locally .
 The successful candidate should be:
 A fast learner who can quickly understand internal procurement processes and systems.
 Comfortable navigating complexity and working across different business cultures and operating models.
 Able to bridge communication and process gaps between the Canadian business and Headquarters.
 Proactive in identifying issues and bringing forward solutions rather than simply processing requests.
 Knowledgeable about local Canadian vendors, commercial practices, and contract management.
 Confident working independently while knowing when to escalate or engage other stakeholders.
 Organized, persistent, and comfortable following up across multiple teams to keep requests moving.
 Commercially minded, practical, and focused on balancing cost, risk, service, and business needs.
 Interested in helping establish and grow a professional procurement function in Canada.
 GROWTH OPPORTUNITY 
 This position is expected to begin on a part-time basis , but it has clear potential to develop into a full-time role as the Canadian business grows and procurement volume increases.
 As the function develops, the successful candidate may take on broader ownership of local sourcing, vendor management, contract lifecycle management, procurement governance, process improvement, and strategic supplier relationships.

 Competitive salary

 The Senior Manager, Global Revenue Controller leads and develops the revenue accounting team and oversees global revenue accounting in accordance with IFRS and company policies. This people manager role combines strong technical accounting expertise, particularly in IFRS 15 and complex customer arrangements, with hands-on financial reporting responsibilities. As a key member of the financial reporting team, the Senior Manager prepares financial statement notes, prepares and reviews technical accounting memos, and partners with regional finance teams and other functions to resolve accounting matters and deliver accurate, timely reporting.
 Key Responsibilities 
 People leadership: Manage and develop direct reports, set priorities, allocate work, review deliverables, and provide coaching and feedback to ensure quality and timely reporting.
 Revenue accounting: Oversee global revenue recognition under IFRS 15, including complex contract assessments, performance obligations, transaction price allocation, and timing of recognition.
 Percentage-of-completion (POC) accounting: Manage POC accounting, including project reviews, revenue recognition, unbilled receivables, and deferred revenue.
 Complex revenue arrangements: Oversee accounting assessments involving non-standard shipping terms, discount incentives, and Software Assurance contracts.
 Close and controls: Oversee revenue-related close activities, journal entries, reconciliations, and unbilled receivable and deferred revenue balances; resolve aged items and discrepancies and maintain effective internal controls and documentation.
 Financial reporting: Prepare financial statement notes, including revenue disclosures, and contribute to broader quarterly and annual financial reporting deliverables.
 Technical accounting: Research complex transactions and accounting issues; prepare and review technical memos documenting IFRS analysis, judgements, and conclusions.
 Business and audit partnership: Partner with Sales, Operations, Legal, regional finance teams, and external auditors to resolve accounting and reporting matters.

 Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field and a CPA designation.
 Progressive experience in technical accounting and financial reporting, including direct people management and team development.
 Strong IFRS expertise, particularly IFRS 15, complex revenue arrangements, and percentage-of-completion (POC) accounting.
 Demonstrated experience preparing financial statement notes and preparing and reviewing technical accounting memos.
 Strong analytical and communication skills, with the ability to explain complex accounting conclusions and collaborate across functions.

 Better Everyday : review every brand moment against its goal, and make the next one bigger, cheaper or better.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Data Science, the Senior Data Analyst - Revenue & Margin will be responsible for owning the analytics infrastructure that turns raw transaction data into cost, revenue, and margin truth. This role supports Finance, Product, and the business through the COGS tracker and cost engine, vendor invoice validation, monthly cost and margin reporting, revenue-to-transaction mapping, and the usage metrics Finance bills customers on every month. This is a technical role first: you'll write production SQL and Python, manage data pipelines, and take an AI-first approach to self-service reporting.

This is a full-time, permanent position based out of our Vancouver office, working on a hybrid model (3 days per week in-office).

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

FINANCIAL DATA LAYER

 - Design, build, and maintain the core financial data layer in the data warehouse: the tables, models, and schemas that COGS, revenue, and margin reporting all depend on.

 - Own data quality and change management for this layer, ensuring new products, vendors, and pricing changes flow through cleanly without breaking downstream cost, revenue, or margin reporting.

COGS TRACKING & COST INFRASTRUCTURE

 - Own and maintain the internally built COGS tracker, including the front-end portal for vendor contract terms and the backend database that stores them.

 - Maintain and extend the Python-based cost engine and its supporting data pipeline, which calculates the exact cost of every transaction run through the Trulioo platform.

VENDOR INVOICING & ACCRUALS

 - Produce monthly invoice reports for every Trulioo data provider, giving Finance what it needs to validate incoming vendor invoices before payment.

 - Support accruals for vendors that invoice less frequently, keeping cost recognition accurate between invoice cycles.

COST & MARGIN REPORTING

 - Build and maintain the suite of monthly cost dashboards and reports used across the business.

 - Own margin reporting, including transaction-level margin data and the metrics and drivers behind it, giving Product a clear view of where to focus margin improvement.

REVENUE INGESTION & UNIT ECONOMICS

 - Build and maintain the pipelines that ingest finalized revenue from Finance and map it back to the transactions that generated it.

 - Partner with Product and Finance to turn this data into unit economics insight that informs pricing, vendor, and product decisions.

MONTHLY BILLING & USAGE METRICS

 - Translate signed customer quotes and frequently changing pricing models into code logic that accurately counts usage for every billed SKU.

 - Deliver monthly usage metrics to Finance for every SKU sold, as part of the monthly invoicing process.

 - Maintain and update usage-counting logic as pricing and product configuration evolve, in close coordination with Sales, Deal Desk, and Product.

AI & EMERGING TECHNOLOGIES

 - Build agents and tooling that expose the cost, revenue, and margin data layer to Finance and Product for self-service, checking outputs against source data so the answers stay trustworthy.
   
   

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field such as Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or Finance, or equivalent experience.

 - 5–7+ years in a data analyst, analytics engineer, or similar technical analytics role.

 - Strong cross-functional communication, translating between engineering and product concepts and financial ones for both Data Science and Finance audiences.

 - Exceptional attention to detail, since your work feeds vendor payments, revenue reporting, and customer invoicing.

 - Ability to go deep on a complex product and its configuration and data patterns.

 - Advanced SQL for writing and troubleshooting complex queries against large transactional datasets.

 - Production Python for building and maintaining data pipelines and business logic, beyond analysis notebooks.

 - Working knowledge of COGS, revenue recognition, margin, and accruals, enough to partner credibly with Finance.

 - Experience with the following tools/technology: Redshift (or an equivalent cloud data warehouse), Airflow (or an equivalent orchestration tool), SQL, and Python.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Core Infrastructure team builds the software systems that power engineering workflows across Cerebras.

Our infrastructure coordinates complex work across machines, clusters, development environments, and hardware systems. We build orchestration frameworks, execution engines, scheduling systems, test infrastructure, developer tools, and reusable software platforms that allow engineers to build, test, qualify, and deliver software reliably at scale.

These systems are primarily built in Python, but the work goes far beyond scripting or automation. Our frameworks act as the control plane for distributed workflows, managing resources, execution state, concurrency, failures, retries, dependencies, and observability across large and complex environments.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring a Software Engineer to design and build the core software behind Cerebras engineering infrastructure.

You will work on Python frameworks, orchestration systems, distributed execution, scheduling, test infrastructure, and developer tooling. You will help define the architecture and APIs that other engineering teams depend on every day.

This role is a strong fit for an engineer who enjoys reading unfamiliar code, understanding how systems fit together, debugging difficult problems, and improving the underlying design rather than applying one-off fixes.

We value strong software-engineering fundamentals, independent problem solving, and sound systems thinking more than familiarity with any particular infrastructure product.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, develop, test, and maintain Python frameworks and services used to orchestrate engineering workflows across machines and clusters.

 - Build reusable abstractions for scheduling, distributed execution, resource management, test execution, workflow planning, and failure recovery.

 - Define clear APIs, module boundaries, extension points, and data models that allow infrastructure systems to evolve without becoming difficult to maintain.

 - Reason about concurrency, asynchronous execution, multiprocessing, state management, retries, idempotency, cancellation, and partial failures.

 - Debug complex issues spanning Python applications, operating systems, processes, filesystems, networking, remote machines, and distributed services.

 - Write high-quality automated tests and documentation for infrastructure that is expected to be reliable and widely reused.

 - Partner with platform, CI, release, quality, ML systems, and product engineering teams to understand requirements and translate them into scalable software designs.

SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

 - 5+ years of professional software-engineering experience.

 - Strong proficiency in Python and a solid understanding of the language’s strengths, limitations, and runtime behavior.

 - Experience designing maintainable software systems, libraries, frameworks, backend services, or developer-facing APIs.

 - Good judgment around software architecture, abstraction boundaries, design patterns, extensibility, and long-term maintainability.

 - Understanding of concurrency concepts such as processes, threads, asynchronous execution, synchronization, and shared state.

 - Foundational understanding of operating systems, including processes, signals, filesystems, resource management, and program execution.

 - Foundational understanding of distributed-systems concepts such as retries, timeouts, idempotency, partial failure, coordination, and eventual consistency.

 - Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, including the ability to form hypotheses, gather evidence, and work through unfamiliar systems independently.

PREFERRED SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with Python concurrency technologies such as asyncio, multiprocessing, concurrent futures, or event-driven systems.

 - Experience building orchestration engines, workflow systems, schedulers, distributed job runners, or control-plane software.

 - Experience developing test infrastructure or extensions for frameworks such as pytest.

 - Familiarity with CI systems, build systems, release infrastructure, or developer-productivity tooling.

 - Experience with Kubernetes, containerized environments, cluster schedulers, or remote execution systems.

 - BS/MS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
